title: Sleep Onset Latency (ISL)
lesson: Sleep onset latency is the elapsed time from lights out to the first sleep epoch. For the same recording interval, latency can also be calculated as TRT − TST − WASO, provided WASO includes wake from sleep onset until lights on, as explicitly defined here.
memoryClue: Latency is the wait from lights out until sleep begins.
coachBobNote: Keep initial sleep latency separate from wake after sleep onset: one occurs before sleep begins, the other after sleep has begun.

workedExample.prompt: TRT is 470 minutes, TST is 390 minutes, and WASO is 55 minutes. Find initial sleep latency.

guided.prompt: The PSG has total recording time (TRT) 480 minutes, total sleep time (TST) 410 minutes, and wake after sleep onset (WASO) 50 minutes through lights on. Calculate sleep onset latency in minutes.
guided.hint: Subtract both sleep and WASO from TRT.

commonErrors.message: That is total wake time. Remove WASO to isolate the wake time before sleep onset.

guided.prompt: The PSG has total recording time (TRT) 450 minutes, total sleep time (TST) 375 minutes, and wake after sleep onset (WASO) 45 minutes through lights on. Calculate sleep onset latency in minutes.
guided.success: Correct. Initial sleep latency is 30 minutes.

definitionNote: PSG calculations in this module use the lights-out to lights-on recording interval and count WASO through lights on (AAST, 2021, §3.3.3.1). Other contexts may use different endpoints or denominators.
